title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-scratchpad-9
content:
Goal: capture commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and quick next steps for the Dedicated GPU pool autoscale/warmup incident (capacity thrash observed).

Context / Symptoms (observed 2024-10-30 14:00-16:30 UTC):
- Pool repeatedly scaled up then down over ~2.5 hours. Apps saw higher tail latency when new requests hit just after node add, then errors when warmup not finished.
- Users hit transient 5xxs for a few minutes during scale cycles.
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale events triggered by short CPU/GPU bursts followed by rapid drop.

Quick timeline (local times approx):
- 14:02: initial spike in queue length -> autoscaler triggered +4 nodes
- 14:05: new nodes registered but pods pending for 30-90s
- 14:07: some pods OOMKilled or FailedMount (see logs) -> autoscaler decided there is leftover capacity -> scaled down
- 14:20: second spike -> +6 nodes -> similar pattern repeats

Commands I ran (raw):
- kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-gpu -o wide\  
  OUTPUT (snippet):
  NAME                                        STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   
  gpu-node-7a2f   Ready    <none>   3h   v1.28.2   10.0.12.45

- kubectl describe node gpu-node-7a2f\  
  EVENTS: 
  Warning  Eviction  2m    kubelet  The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage. Container runtime flagged slow removal of old images.

- kubectl logs -n infra autoscaler-deployment-5 -f\  
  ERROR (snippet): autoscaler: scale decision: add=4 remove=6 based on utilization 0.78 (threshold 0.65)
  DEBUG: evaluation window=60s -> short spikes dominate decision

- kubectl logs -n serving runtime-pod-xyz -c init-model-fetch\  
  ERROR: s3 fetch failed: AccessDenied: "Access Denied"
  at request send (s3client.go:222)
  
- dmesg on node after OOM: "Out of memory: Killed process 4123 (python) total-vm: 12500000kB, anon-rss: 11000000kB"

- Prometheus queries (via grafana):
  - rate(gpu_pod_startup_time_seconds[5m]) shows spike at 14:03 -> 45s avg startup vs baseline 8s
  - sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pool="dedicated"}[1m])) / sum(machine_cpu_cores{pool="dedicated"}) -> very spiky, oscillates between 0.12 and 0.85

Error snippets captured: 
- "failed to pull image \"gcr.io/redwood/models:1.2.3\": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to resolve reference"
- "OOMKilled: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space"
- "Failed scheduling pod: 0/8 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" (but GPUs were available after nodes joined)
- "s3 fetch failed: AccessDenied" on init container -> causes longer init times -> delays readiness
- "evicted: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage" -> some warmup/cache images might be evicted during heavy churn

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Short-burst sensitive autoscaler: evaluation window too short, reacts to transient bursts (60s) causing scale oscillation. Need smoothing / stabilization.
2) Warmup path fragile: init-container fetching model artifacts from S3 sometimes failing (AccessDenied), leading to longer startup; autoscaler sees pending pods and scales more. Intermittent IAM token refresh issue or S3 throttling.
3) Node resource pressure on ephemeral-storage and memory: images/weights eviction and OOMs cause pods to fail on first start -> autoscaler counts them as capacity still needed -> more nodes added -> thrash.
4) Pod resource requests/limits mismatch: requests too small/limits too big (or vice-versa) causing scheduler to mis-evaluate fit and causing packing inefficiencies.
5) Autoscaler config defaults: scale-down delay too short or permissive thresholds for removing nodes.

What I changed / attempted (quick mitigations):
- Increased autoscaler scale_up_cooldown from 60s -> 180s in staging to test (did not deploy to prod yet).
- Temporarily bumped pool min_size from 2 -> 5 (reduced immediate tail errors) at 14:40 but increased cost.
- Deployed a small pre-warm DaemonSet (init prefetcher) that pulls model blob to node-local cache on node join to reduce init container latency (testing in canary pool).
- Added retry in init-model-fetch with exponential backoff for S3 (observed AccessDenied probably transient and retried succeeds)

Notes on warmup behavior:
- Warmup happens in two phases: 1) fetch artifacts (init container) ~8-40s (variable), 2) model load into GPU memory (~2-20s depending on quantization and kernel selection).
- When init container fails, pod stays Pending/Init and is not counted as ready; autoscaler sees backlog and scales. If failures are due to node resource pressure (eviction), repeated attempts create churn.

Observations from logs correlating events:
- 14:03: s3 AccessDenied spikes -> correlated with a short spike in AWS STS error rate in infra logs (possible rate-limiting on role assumption).
- 14:06: node kubelet reported image GC taking 40s -> correlated with ephemeral-storage eviction.
- 14:09: several pods show OOMKilled while loading model weights -> probably memory bump during load (we don't reserve enough overhead in request).

Potential fixes (short->long term):
- Short term: raise pool min_size (safety buffer), increase scale_up window/cooldown, increase scale-down stabilization window to avoid flip-flop.
- Fix init-container reliability: add retries, better error logging, ensure S3 IAM role usage not hitting STS rate limits (consider longer role caching).
- Pre-warm image/model: run lightweight DaemonSet to prefetch blobs to node-local cache on join, or use a node-init sidecar that mounts shared cache.
- Review pod requests/limits: pad memory requests to account for peak model load (e.g., +20% during weight map).
- Tweak scheduler bin-packing labels: ensure we use node labels to group similar workloads to avoid fragmentation.
- Consider moving warmup to a pooled pre-warmed process that holds model in GPU memory for a few minutes (keeps cost but reduces latency).

Instrumentation gaps / next data to collect:
- precise distribution of init-container durations with status (success vs AccessDenied).
- per-node ephemeral-storage usage patterns around node join/leave.
- STS / IAM error counts for role assumption correlated with node add times.
- detailed OOM logs from kubelet for the OOMKilled processes (container vs host).

Immediate next steps (mine):
- Add grafana panel for init-container duration by image/model and success vs failure (ticketed INF-790).
- Push small patch to init-model-fetch to add exponential backoff + longer jittered retries (PR drafted: see linked GH).
- Coordinate with infra on STS rate limits and S3 IAM usage (pinged @Ibrahim).
- Roll out pre-warm DaemonSet to canary pool and monitor startup times.

Open questions: 
- Are we using scale-to-zero for this pool by default? (if yes, that worsens warmup)
- Do other pools exhibit similar AccessDenied patterns or is it specific to this pool's IAM role?
- Should we allow a short lived warm pool (min nodes > 0) for high priority customers?

Scratch CLI snippets to reproduce / debug (keep for later):
- kubectl get pods -n serving -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,INIT:.status.initContainerStatuses[*].state --selector=app=model-server
- kubectl exec -it node/gpu-node-7a2f -- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i evict
- aws sts get-caller-identity --profile infra-deployer (check role caching on the infra tokens)
- curl -s "http://grafana.internal/api/ds/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{query: "rate(gpu_pod_startup_time_seconds[5m])"}'

Final note: this doc is my working breadcrumbs; will turn into a short incident postmortem draft after we stabilize and collect the extra metrics above.

-- Maya
